title: Anticipatory admission controller with priority decay for cross-region burst smoothing
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem statement:

We continue to see operational pain during sudden client-originated bursts that span multiple regions. Existing token-bucket + soft-fallback policies react only after burst pressure manifests (queue growth, SLO violations, or limiter outage). This leads to repeated transient SLO misses and uncoordinated shedding across regions. Current approaches either favor strict global throttling (poor tail latency for important tenants) or local elastic shedding (unfairness across tenants, repeated retries).

Proposal summary:

Implement an Anticipatory Admission Controller (AAC) that: 1) observes short-term request arrival patterns per-tenant and per-route, 2) uses a lightweight predictive window to forecast imminent burst pressure, and 3) applies preemptive admission rules with a priority-decay model to gracefully smooth cross-region bursts. The AAC is a hybrid layer that sits ahead of local token-buckets and coordinates soft leases between regions for tenants with high SLO priority.

Core design elements (high level):

- Predictive window: exponentially-weighted short histogram (0-30s) that estimates arrival rate slope and variance per tenant/route. No ML model dependency; heuristics tuned by existing telemetry.
- Admission policy tiers: allow, deprioritize, pre-shed. Decisions map to token admission weights (full token / fractional weight / immediate rejection-with-backoff).
- Priority decay: tenants have an instant priority score that decays over a 5–120s half-life depending on service tier. This prevents priority starvation and reduces oscillation where one tenant permanently blocks others after a burst.
- Cross-region soft leases: when a region predicts sustained burst, it can request short-lived admission leases from peer regions (lease metadata is small: tenant, route, weight delta, expiry). Leases are opportunistic and revoke-able; they do not require strict consensus to avoid global blocking.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Simulated multi-region burst test shows 30–60% reduction in SLO p99 tail spikes for high-priority tenants compared to current baseline without increasing total rejected requests by >10%.
2) Fairness metric (Jain index over token grants) improves for medium-priority tenants during bursts.
3) No persistent priority inversion: after a simulated burst, all tenants recover to baseline success rates within 90s.
4) Feature toggles allow region-local only operation and full cross-region mode.
5) Monitoring alerts added for lease-creation rate, pre-shed rate, prediction error, and priority starvation signals.
implementation_notes:
Phase A (local predictive admission): implement predictive window and admission mapping into local admission controllers. Phase B (soft leases): add lease protocol over existing control-plane pubsub (stateless messages with idempotency). Phase C (tuning & rollout): closed beta with a subset of high-SLA tenants and synthetic traffic rig.

Interactions with circuit breakers and existing limiter fabric:
- AAC must respect active circuit breaker states: if a CB is open for a tenant, AAC does not grant leases for that tenant and prioritizes recovery traffic.
- AAC's pre-shed should trigger a graded circuit-breaker evaluation and increment CB counters (so post-mortem links exist).
- During limiter outages AAC falls back to conservative local admission (deny-by-default for new leases) and emits an operational runbook step to enable emergency shedding policies.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for predictive window calculations and priority decay math.
- Deterministic integration tests for admission outcomes against synthetic arrival patterns.
- Multi-region simulator (k6 + local runtime harness) that replays production arrival traces and injects region network partitions to validate lease revocation and recovery.
- Chaos scenario: limiter process crash + restart while AAC active to validate fallback behaviour.
- Perf test: measure AAC CPU/memory overhead at 100k QPS per region; ensure <2% p99 increase in processing latency.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy AAC behind a feature flag, region-local only, on a canary slice (5% of traffic) for 48h.
2) Gradually enable cross-region leases for a set of non-critical tenants (10% of SLA weight) while monitoring SLOs and lease churn.
3) Expand to high-SLA tenants after 2 successful weeks of stability and manual sign-off from SRE/PM.
4) Full global rollout with automatic tuning agent active to converge decay half-life and pre-shed thresholds.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Primary metrics: predicted arrival slope, prediction error rate, lease-grant-rate, pre-shed-rate, per-tenant admission-weight, priority-decay-distribution.
Alerting rules:
- prediction_error > 25% for >2m for any tenant (SEV1)
- pre-shed_rate exceeds baseline + 3 sigma (SEV1)
- lease_revocation_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m (SEV2)
- p99 latency regression > 10% for high-SLA tenants (SEV1)
updates: 2026-02-12: Initial spike analysis and design sketch. Found repeating pattern of cross-region correlated bursts caused by scheduled batch jobs that throttle upstream - confirmed with infra logs.
2026-02-20: Prototype predictive window implemented in dev environment; early signals show prediction lead time of ~4–8s on replayed traces.
2026-03-01: Design review with SRE and Runtime teams. Requested ability to operate AAC in read-only observability mode and explicit opt-in per-customer. Diego to add feature flag gating.

2026-03-08: Simulation runs (multi-region) completed: median p99 improvement 38% for top 10 tenants; pre-shed rate peaked at 6% during extreme bursts. Need to tighten priority-decay for tier-3 tenants.
2026-03-12: Security reviewed lease message schema; no PII and messages are signed. Security recommended TTL < 20s and replay protection. Marking ticket In Progress for Phase A work.
2026-03-12: Assigned implementation work to Diego (runtime admission) and Priya (control-plane lease plumbing) and scheduled integration tests in Cycle 2026-W10.
comments: PM (Lena Ortiz): Please include a kill-switch that immediately disables cross-region leases if SLOs regress for any tenant by >10%.
SRE (Marco Li): Ensure lease requests are best-effort; do not block local fast-path. Also add detailed tracing to follow a lease lifecycle for debugging outages.
Design (Camille Park): UX request: expose per-tenant decay half-life in Console under Advanced Rate Controls so customer support can advise on tuning.
Review (Diego Martinez): Prototype shows modest CPU impact; will instrument and cap evictions to avoid CPU-induced flapping.
